newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes just easier, hemmed in range.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes just easier, hemmed in range.

text.p: Gold prices were marooned at slightly lower levels on Friday ahead of the month end, Easter holiday and OTC option expiry.
"If it wasn't so quiet it would be quite an interesting time with all these factors coming next week," one dealer said.
As it was, gold fixed at $351.70 per ounce compared with $352.00 on Thursday afternoon when it closed at $351.40/$351.90.
Business was thin in Europe after dollar-yen issues encouraged Japanese selling which weakened the price in Tokyo and Hong Kong.
What might have resulted in a Comex-led rally shortly after the exchange opened was truncated by U.S. Reserve Board chairman Alan Greenspan strongly hinting at upcoming rises in U.S. interest rates.
The monetary policy advising Federal Open market Committee (FOMC) meets next week and a 25 basis point rise has been forecast.
"Unless there is much bigger rate rise than that, gold should be unaffected," one dealer said.
Meanwhile gold was forecast to remain fairly whippy but confined to a tight range bounded by $350.00-$355.00 at the outside.
Mild bullishness earlier in the week after gold showed it had ample physical support to hold it above $345 has dissipated, dealers said.
"The feeling is that after the options expire, the price will move lower, but there is no keen view," a dealer said.
Palladium recovered some lost ground by the time Europe opened after being hit by currency related selling by Japanese speculators, dealers said.
"It is undecided in direction on a mixture of worries about the Russian situation and watching gold," one dealer said.
Dealers said they had seen no moves to suggest Russia's first platinum and palladium shipments of the year would happen this month.
Platinum was less affected and shed $1.95 from the close to $338.00/$379.00.
Dealers said technically and fundamentally platinum was regarded positively and a move through $381-$382 could take it into the low $390s.
Silver was pretty quiet on a three-cent gain to $5.20/$5.22.
